e1a027308f2f9d5ea465e91f26764f17ef3d01a0.note: Re-triaged per task-5's Step 5: no honest fixture is possible without fabricating a vendor RPC no supported agent speaks. Prevents prompting into a session that is "visibly mid a self-continued turn" (an open tool call, or stream traffic within 3s, with no prompt of ours outstanding) by cancelling first. That decision point cannot arise in session.rs's turn loop: it does drain any backlog sitting in `incoming` before sending the next `session/prompt` (added by this PR, for `prompt_stall`'s "first sign of life" bound) — so notifications are read in the brief gap before a prompt goes out too, not only while one is outstanding. But that drain is unconditional: it forwards whatever backlog exists through the ordinary decode and then ALWAYS sends the next prompt immediately after, with no branch that inspects the backlog to decide whether the session "looks busy" first. A queued steer is only ever dispatched once the previous drive_turn call has already returned (session.rs: "Steering rides the turn boundary, always"), so there is no code path here that could act on "visibly busy" evidence even now that notifications are read slightly earlier. A fixture posing this scenario would have to add a decision the production loop does not make.
